sentences.text:
This fourth application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.05 of 2022 registered at Police Station Cyber Kampoo, District Gwalior (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471,
204 of IPC and added Sections 66-C, and 66-D of I.T. Act.

entities.text: Police Station Cyber Kampoo, District Gwalior
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 19.10.2022.

First application was dismissed as withdrawn by Coordinate Bench of this Court v i d e o r d e r dated 14.12.2022 passed in MCRC No.56922/2022, second application was dismissed as withdrawn by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 21.04.2023 passed in MCRC No.16015/2023 and third application was dismissed as withdrawn by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 15.09.2023 passed in MCRC No.37987/2023.
After rejection of earlier bail applications, prosecution witnesses have been examined.

As per the case of prosecution, Sudhish Singh Tomar submitted a written complaint on 17.11.2021 to the Superintendent of Police, State Cyber Police 2 MCRC-18393-2024 Zone, Gwalior with regard to fraudulent withdrawn of Rs.6,23,989/- from the account of his father Tehsildar Singh Tomar in SBI,
Morena Branch.
It is stated in the complaint that Tehsildar Singh Tomar, retired Teacher has an account in SBI, Morena Branch, wherein his pension is regularly deposited.
Tehsildar Singh found that Rs.6,23,989/- has been withdrawn from his account without any intimation.
On such allegations, the matter was enquired.
It was found that the amount was transferred into the account of Dilshad, Samad, Farooz, Ruksina and Harjeet.
Dilshad was arrested on 20.08.2022.

He informed in his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act that Tehrim S/o Irfhan used to provide him mobile SIMs registered in fake names and using these mobile SIMs, he used to call innocent depositors and withdraw amount from their bank accounts.

sentences.text: Rajat Lodhi in his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act informed that Chandrashekhar @ Chandu (applicant), Namdev and Vivek Kumar were working as agents of Vodafone and Idea.
He approached Chandrashekar and Vivek for issuance of SIM in fake names.
Chandrashekhar and Vivek provided him SIMs issued registered in fake names.
He gave those SIMS to Tehrim.
Tehrim paid him Rs.1,10,000/- out of which, he has paid Rs.20,000/- each to Vivek and Chandrashekhar.
Accordingly, Chandrashekhar was arrested on 19.10.2022.
In his statement recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, he informed that he used to register mobile SIM of Vodafone and Idea and provide them to Rajat Lodhi.
Applicant is in judicial custody ever since.
On completion of investigation, final report was submitted.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the matter merely on suspicion and for issuance of SIM.
Applicant has issued SIM 3 MCRC-18393-2024 but he was not aware of alleged offence.
He never came in contact with main accused Tehrim and Dilshad.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that all material witnesses have been examined.
No offence as alleged is made out against applicant.
Applicant has already undergone custody for one year and nine months.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is aged around 35 years and is Shopkeeper by profession.
He is sole bread earner of the family, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family, home and profession.
There is no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence by applicant.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant.
The trial would take time to complete.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
